title: Conormal fibre sequence for a smooth closed subscheme
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of $k$-schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-scheme-over-base], with $Z$ smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Write $\Omega_{X/k}$ and $\Omega_{Z/k}$ for the relative differential sheaves [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. For $z\in Z$, set $x=i(z)$, $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $S=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, $I=\ker(R\twoheadrightarrow S)$ and $\kappa=\kappa(z)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Then the canonical sequence of $\kappa$-vector spaces
$$0\longrightarrow (I/I^2)\otimes_S\kappa\longrightarrow \Omega_{X/k,x}\otimes_R\kappa\longrightarrow \Omega_{Z/k,z}\otimes_S\kappa\longrightarrow0$$
is exact. The first arrow sends $(f\bmod I^2)\otimes1$ to $df\otimes1$ for every $f\in I$; the second is induced by the local-ring map $R\to S$. Here $I/I^2$ is the quotient of $I$ by the submodule generated by products of two elements of $I$, and the tensors are module base changes [def-weil-module-base-change].

source.place: Tag 06AA (lemma-differentials-relative-immersion-smooth): short exact conormal sequence for an immersion with source smooth over the base; passage to the residue field preserves exactness because the smooth differential sheaf on Z is locally free (Tag 02G1, lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free).

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ containing $x$. The affine closed-immersion criterion gives $V=i^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, with a surjective $k$-algebra map $A\twoheadrightarrow B$; write $J$ for its kernel and identify $B=A/J$. Put $N=J/J^2$, $M=B\otimes_A\Omega_{A/k}$ and $P=\Omega_{B/k}$. The $B$-action on $N$ is $\bar a[j]=[aj]$: changing a lift $a$ adds an element of $J^2$.

source.place: Tag 01QO, lemma-closed-immersion; Tag 06AA, lemma-differentials-relative-immersion-smooth, reduction to affines

proof.text: Set $C=A/J^2$ and $K=J/J^2\subset C$. The kernel of $C\twoheadrightarrow B$ is $K$ and $K^2=0$, so $T=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset T'=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is a first order thickening of affine $k$-schemes. Smoothness of $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, in its infinitesimal lifting definition, lifts the inclusion $T=V\to Z$ to a $k$-morphism $h:T'\to Z$. Every point of $T'$ lies in $T$ topologically, since every prime contains $K$ (if $u^2=0$ then $u$ belongs to every prime). Thus $h^{-1}(V)=T'$. Restricting its continuous map and structure-sheaf map to the open subspace $V$ factors $h$ through $V$. Under the affine spectrum correspondence this factorization is a $k$-algebra map $\sigma:B\to C$ such that $\pi\sigma=\mathrm{id}_B$, where $\pi:C\to B$ is the quotient. This applies the lifting property to the affine test schemes $T,T'$, and does not assume that a localized smooth algebra is finitely presented.

source.place: Tags 04EX (definition-thickening) and 02H0 (definition-formally-smooth); the square-zero lifting used in the proof of Algebra Tag 02HP

proof.text: Apply the quotient differential sequence to $k\to A\to A/J=B$. It supplies well-defined $B$-linear maps $\delta:N\to M$, $[j]\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm dj$, and $w:M\to P$, $b\otimes\mathrm da\mapsto b\,\mathrm d\bar a$, with $w$ surjective and $\ker w=\operatorname{im}\delta$. The cited statement gives precisely this right exactness; injectivity of $\delta$ is proved next.

source.place: Tag 00RU, lemma-differential-seq, including the formulas for both maps

proof.text: For $a\in A$ define $D(a)=(a\bmod J^2)-\sigma(\bar a)\in K=N$. It is additive and zero on $k$. In $C$ write $a\bmod J^2=\sigma(\bar a)+D(a)$. Since $K^2=0$, multiplication gives $D(ab)=\sigma(\bar a)D(b)+\sigma(\bar b)D(a)=\bar aD(b)+\bar bD(a)$, where $C$ acts on $K$ through $B$. Thus $D$ is a $k$-derivation into the $A$-module $N$. The universal property of differentials gives a map $\Omega_{A/k}\to N$, and because $JN=0$ it extends to the $B$-linear map $\tau:M\to N$, $b\otimes\mathrm da\mapsto bD(a)$. For $j\in J$, $D(j)=[j]$, hence $\tau\delta=\mathrm{id}_N$.

source.place: Tag 02HP, lemma-differential-seq-split, derivation in the proof, applied after the square-zero lift; computation expanded

proof.text: The previous two steps give an explicit splitting. For $p\in P$, choose $m\in M$ with $w(m)=p$ and set $s(p)=m-\delta\tau(m)$. If $m'$ is another lift, $m-m'=\delta(n)$ for some $n\in N$, so the two values differ by $\delta(n)-\delta\tau\delta(n)=0$. This also proves that $s$ is $B$-linear. We have $ws=\mathrm{id}_P$, $\tau s=0$ and $\delta\tau+sw=\mathrm{id}_M$. Consequently $M\cong N\oplus P$, by $m\mapsto(\tau m,wm)$ with inverse $(n,p)\mapsto\delta n+sp$.

source.place: Tag 06A8, lemma-differential-seq-smooth: split exactness, expanded by the retraction and the quotient sequence rather than used as a black box

proof.text: Give $\kappa=\kappa(z)$ its $B$-algebra structure through the germ map $B\to S$ and the residue map $S\to\kappa$. Tensor the four splitting identities of the preceding step with $\kappa$ over $B$. Functoriality of module base change preserves sums, composites and identities, so $\delta\otimes1$ still has left inverse $\tau\otimes1$, $w\otimes1$ still has right inverse $s\otimes1$, and $(\delta\otimes1)(\tau\otimes1)+(s\otimes1)(w\otimes1)=\mathrm{id}$. For $v\in\ker(w\otimes1)$ this last identity gives $v=(\delta\otimes1)(\tau\otimes1)(v)$. Thus $0\to N\otimes_B\kappa\to M\otimes_B\kappa\to P\otimes_B\kappa\to0$ is exact. No flatness of $\kappa$ over $B$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 06A8, lemma-differential-seq-smooth, split exactness; passage to an arbitrary module base change by the displayed splitting identities

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ correspond to $z$ and let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be its inverse image. The affine stalk and Spec-map stalk formulas identify $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$, $S=B_{\mathfrak q}$ and $R\to S$ with $a/t\mapsto\bar a/\bar t$. The quotient-localization lemma gives $I=JR$ and $S=R/I$. Products of fractions show $I^2=J^2R$. Hence $(J/J^2)_{\mathfrak q}\cong I/I^2$ by $[j]/\bar t\mapsto[j/t]$. To check the inverse, every element of $I$ is $j/t$ after taking a common denominator; if $j/t\in J^2R$, clearing the finitely many denominators gives $u j\in J^2$ for some $u\notin\mathfrak p$, exactly the condition $[j]/\bar t=0$ in the localized quotient. Balancing gives $N\otimes_B\kappa\cong(I/I^2)\otimes_S\kappa$: denominators $\bar t\notin\mathfrak q$ act by units on $\kappa$, so the inverse to inserting the localization sends $([j]/\bar t)\otimes c$ to $[j]\otimes\bar t^{-1}c$.

source.place: Tag 00CT, proposition-localize-quotient; Schemes Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (6); conormal localization and tensor identification checked on fractions

proof.text: The affine description of the relative differential sheaf and the tilde-stalk localization formula identify $\Omega_{X/k,x}=(\Omega_{A/k})_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\Omega_{Z/k,z}=(\Omega_{B/k})_{\mathfrak q}$, with $\mathrm da$ corresponding to the germ of $\mathrm da$. Thus $M\otimes_B\kappa\cong\Omega_{X/k,x}\otimes_R\kappa$ by $(b\otimes\eta)\otimes c\mapsto\eta_x\otimes\bar b c$, and $P\otimes_B\kappa\cong\Omega_{Z/k,z}\otimes_S\kappa$ by $\eta\otimes c\mapsto\eta_z\otimes c$. Their inverses clear denominators as in the preceding step, e.g. $(\eta/t)\otimes c\mapsto(1\otimes\eta)\otimes\bar t^{-1}c$. Under these identifications the arrows of the exact sequence in step 6 are the asserted canonical arrows. In particular, write $f\in I$ as $j/t$ with $j\in J$, $t\notin\mathfrak p$. The Leibniz rule gives $\mathrm d(j/t)=t^{-1}\mathrm dj-jt^{-2}\mathrm dt$; the second term vanishes after tensoring with $\kappa$ because $j$ has zero residue. The first arrow therefore sends $[f]\otimes1$ to $\mathrm df\otimes1$. The second arrow sends the germ of $\mathrm da$ to the germ of $\mathrm d\bar a$, and respects the same denominator rule, so it is exactly the map induced by $R\to S$. This proves every clause.

X is arbitrary, Z is smooth and z need not be closed; both arrows are stated. I tested it on four cases: Spec k inside the dual numbers (characteristic 2 too), the origin of the cuspidal cubic y^2=x^3, the generic point of a line in A^2, and J=0. Step 1 uses parts (1) and (2) of the closed-immersion criterion leaf. Step 2 lifts through the formal-smoothness clause of def-sbc-smooth-morphisms on the affine first-order thickening Spec B in Spec A/J^2. The lift factors through V because K is nilpotent, and pi sigma = id. Step 3 is the Jacobi-Zariski leaf with (k,A,J); only the right exactness is taken from it. Step 4 is the 02HP derivation D(a)=(a mod J^2)-sigma(a-bar) (algebra.tex:34158); I checked the product calculation and tau delta = id. Steps 5-6 give the splitting identities, which survive tensoring with kappa by functoriality, so no flatness is needed. Step 7 is correct: affine-open stalk (c), the Spec-map stalk lemma and quotient localization give I=JR, and I checked the inverse of the conormal localization map. Step 8 is correct: tilde stalks identify the differentials, and d(j/t)=t^-1 dj - j t^-2 dt gives the first-arrow formula. proof_deps equals the union of the uses, and there is no cycle.
